title: Deep Work, lesson 1 - why busy days feel empty

slides.title: Deep Work
slides.sub: why your busiest days feel empty

slides.title: Why Your Busiest Days Feel Empty
body: You answered emails. Sat in meetings. Replied to every ping.
You were **busy all day.**
But the work that *actually matters* didn't move.
Here's why, and how to fix it.

slides.title: It Starts With Two Kinds Of Work
body: Cal Newport splits work in two:

list: **Shallow work:** emails and logistics you can do half asleep.
**Deep work:** focusing without distraction on something hard.

body: Shallow work keeps you busy. It *rarely creates anything new.*

slides.title: Every Switch Leaves Something Behind

graphic.caption: your attention, right after a quick check (illustration)

body: Researcher Sophie Leroy found that when you switch tasks, part of your attention **stays stuck** on the last one.
She called it _attention residue._
Even a quick inbox check leaves a *lingering fog.*

slides.title: So Your Focus Never Fully Arrives
body: For example:

list: You go back to your report
Part of you is still in the inbox
The report gets a fraction of you

body: Repeat that all day, and **deep work never starts.**

slides.title: Meanwhile, Work Is Changing Fast
body: Newport argues smart machines are reshaping who gets ahead, drawing on economists Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee.
Two groups thrive:

list: People who work well **alongside complex technology**
**Stars** whose best work can now reach clients anywhere

slides.title: Two Abilities Decide Who Gets Ahead

list: **Learn hard things quickly**, because tools keep changing.
**Produce at an elite level**, in both quality and speed.

body: Both depend on one thing: *deep focus.*

slides.title: That Makes Focus Your Biggest Edge
body: Most people are **constantly connected** and frequently interrupted.
So deep work is becoming *rare* exactly as it becomes *more valuable.*
That gap is your opportunity.

slides.title: Use The Focus Formula

graphic.note: cut either one, and output shrinks

body.try: “I'll work one hour with zero distractions.”

body: One **truly focused hour** can beat several distracted ones.

slides.title: Example: From Spreadsheets To Software
body: Jason Benn's finance job was mostly **spreadsheet work**. He realised much of it could be automated.
So he taught himself to code through *long, intense, undistracted* study sessions.
Result: a job as a **software developer.**

slides.title: Start With One Protected Hour
body: Make it a specific rule:

body.big: IF it's 9:00, THEN my phone goes in another room and I start my hardest task.

body: Same time, **every day.**

slides.title: Measure Your Real Focus
body: Look at yesterday honestly. How many hours of **true, unbroken focus** did you get?
Write the number down.
Then protect *one more hour* tomorrow.

slides.title: Save This For Your Next Busy Day
body: Busy isn't the same as productive.
**Protect one hour. Do the hard thing. Repeat.**
